h1: Indian e-Visa refused? Why it happens and how to avoid it
intro: Had an Indian e-Visa refused, or worried you might? Most refusals come down to a handful of avoidable mistakes. Here are the common ones we see, and how to get it right first time.

sections.heading: 1. Photo problems
sections.text: Shadows, glasses, dark or patterned backgrounds and photos that aren’t square are the most common issues. [See the photo rules](/indian-visa-photo-requirements/).

sections.heading: 2. Details that don’t match
sections.text: Your name, date of birth and passport number must match your passport exactly, including middle names.

sections.heading: 3. Indian e-Visa refused because you weren’t eligible
sections.text: People of Pakistani origin and anyone with a military or police background need a [regular visa](/indian-regular-visa/). Applying for an e-Visa anyway usually ends in a refusal and a lost fee.

sections.heading: 4. Missing documents
sections.text: Business visas need a business card or invitation, medical visas a hospital letter, and so on. Check what your e-Visa needs before you apply.

sections.heading: 5. Previous refusals not declared
sections.text: If you’ve had a visa refused before, for India or anywhere else, say so on the form. Leaving it out can lead to a refusal even if everything else is right.

sections.heading: What to do if your Indian e-Visa is refused
sections.text: There’s no appeal, but you can apply again once the problem is fixed. If an e-Visa isn’t right for you, apply for a regular visa instead. Send us your refusal email and we’ll work out the likely reason and help you reapply. [Read our full guide](/indian-evisa-rejected/).

faqs.q: Can I appeal if my Indian e-Visa is refused?
faqs.a: No. There’s no appeal, but you can make a new application.

faqs.q: Will I get my fee back?
faqs.a: No, the government fee isn’t refundable.
Usually straight away, once you’ve fixed the problem.
